sentences.text: Angoumeius was a member of the class Chondrichthyes, a group that includes sharks and rays.
This animal belongs to the family Dalatiidae, which contains modern mako and porbeagle sharks.
The genus is named after its type locality in Angoumé, France.
Scientists know the animal from many isolated teeth found in the Lutetian stage.
There are seven recorded fossil occurrences of Angoumeius in total.
The species lived from the Danian to the Bartonian, spanning 66 to 37.71 million years ago.
It is debated whether the unusual dentition of Angoumeius allows for a certain familial placement and relationship with other genera.
Researchers suggest Angoumeius may be closely related to Kitefin or Sleeper sharks.
